item.title: SpaceNukes Opens New Facility to Build Next-Gen Space Nuclear Reactors
item.description: Facility Purpose SpaceNukes opened its Manufacture and Materials Development Facility in Los Alamos on Nov. 13, 2026. The site focuses on manufacturing and materials development for the company's Generation 2 space reactor, including additive manufacturing of refractory alloys. No radioactive material is handled at this location. Technical Challenges The next-generation reactor is designed to operate at significantly higher temperatures, which allows for a much smaller radiator to shed heat. However, traditional nickel-based superalloys have reached their limits, forcing the company to transition to refractory metals such as tungsten, molybdenum, and niobium. These metals are notoriously difficult to form and machine using conventional methods. Timeline and Context Led by manufacturing director Omar Mireles, the facility complements the company's testing site in Ohio. This opening follows an agreement with DARPA in October 2026 to design and ground-test a Kilopower reactor, as SpaceNukes pushes toward its goal of flying a nuclear reactor by 2028.

item.title: How ocean carbon storage works during ice ages
item.description: According to MIT Climate: Background Over the past 800,000 years, Earth's climate has swung between warm periods and ice ages driven by orbital shifts and changing greenhouse gas levels. Scientists study how carbon is exchanged between the atmosphere and the ocean to better understand future climate scenarios. Research Details Researchers used a climate model to study Southern Ocean processes, including seawater cooling, sea-ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes. Traditionally, scientists studied these mechanisms independently to isolate cause and effect. However, when run separately, sea ice or glacial circulation alone showed little to no carbon drawdown, and solubility changes alone did not account for the results. When the researchers ran a full experiment coupling sea ice, circulation, and cooling, they observed significant carbon dioxide drawdown and a heavy concentration in the disequilibrium carbon pool. Implications The findings suggest that coupled physical processes are key drivers of ice age ocean carbon storage. When sea ice and circulation act together, they significantly reduce the exposure time of upwelled deep ocean water to the atmosphere, trapping carbon inside the ocean. Additionally, the researchers noted that changes in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation can alter water mass boundaries, affecting how carbon escapes.

item.title: Tech figures petition for Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO
item.description:
Background and Petition
A petition began circulating on social media to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, drawing notable signatories including Elon Musk, researchers, and venture capitalists from firms like Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital. These supporters have a financial and strategic interest in open-source AI, as Huang previously acted as a key defender of open models against regulatory concerns and competition fears regarding China. Challenges and Chip Access
Huang's potential reinstatement faces steep obstacles. Former OpenAI researcher Will DePue published unverified findings suggesting that Chinese AI companies had substantial access to advanced Nvidia Blackwell chips, complicating Nvidia's compliance with U.S. export controls. Additionally, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Nvidia should not replace Huang with an internal candidate, and new rules from the U.S. Department of Commerce aim to limit remote access to AI chips in third-party data centers, which could impact the progress of open-source models.

item.title: Clean data was never enough: How IFS Copperleaf taught AI its business with Databricks Genie One
item.description: According to Databricks: The shift from manual modeling традиционно, companies spend months or years manually cleaning and modeling data from dozens of source systems before applying analytics. IFS Copperleaf’s technology team decided to do a complete 180. They fully modeled only high-stakes areas like finance and sales, letting AI work directly on raw data for everything else. This allowed them to deliver useful insights months faster. Empowering business users for governance Instead of restricting data definitions to a technical team, IFS Copperleaf allowed business users to define metrics and correct AI answers in conversation. Every user-written definition is assigned a named owner and must be approved by an AI Council before company-wide promotion. Security is strictly maintained using Databricks Unity Catalog, ensuring users can only access data they are authorized to see. Real-world impact and adoption Launched company-wide after a ten-month build, IONA achieved a 70% activation rate and strong repeat usage. Employees across marketing, finance, customer success, and HR use IONA via various interfaces like the Genie mobile app, Microsoft Teams, and Claude MCP plugins to automate tasks ranging from pipeline analysis to customer meeting preparation and IT access requests.

item.title: From tasks to goals: How AI agents are changing
item.description:
According to LangChain Blog:
LangChain founder Harrison Chase outlines a fundamental shift in how humans interact with AI agents: moving from specific tasks (like writing an email) to broad goals (like maintaining a blog). Under the hood, this means specifying outcomes rather than actions, and handling ongoing responsibilities rather than bounded assignments.
Key practical shifts include agents needing the creativity to brainstorm tasks, unpredictable tool usage that requires stricter controls, and background execution mechanisms like triggers and stopping rules. Furthermore, memory becomes crucial because the agent must carry forward past decisions and user feedback across multiple runs without constant human repetition.

item.title: UK Defence Ministry defends Starshield use amid monopoly worries
item.description: Background Questions regarding the UK's reliance on commercial satellite networks arose in parliament, driven by concerns over restrictions placed on Ukraine's access to SpaceX services. Liberal Democrat MPs Helen Maguire and James MacCleary raised queries concerning strategic autonomy and the potential loss of access to Starlink and Starshield. Official Response Defence minister Luke Pollard clarified that while Starlink is not used for UK military operations, the Ministry of Defence does use Starshield. Pollard declined to disclose the specific number of Starshield terminals procured, citing national security, but stressed that the service operates alongside other capabilities to ensure operational resilience. Industry Concerns Previous parliamentary reports, including a 2024 House of Lords committee document, have highlighted both the operational advantages and the potential risks of relying on commercial providers during conflicts, particularly regarding service continuity and accountability.

item.title: Why Britain struggles to manufacture the future it invents
item.description: The Innovation Paradox Britain has a long history of industrial pioneering and remains a global hub for additive manufacturing research, backed by major academic institutes. However, statistics show a gap between invention and local commercial production. While British researchers generate thousands of patents, much of the actual manufacturing and component supply often shifts overseas, leaving local machinists and startups fighting for steady domestic orders. Funding and Commercialization Founders of UK-based 3D printing startups report that while government innovation grants help develop early technology, they fail to support the broader commercialization process. Turning a working prototype into a reliable product requires solving training, maintenance, and customer validation issues, which demands capital that grants rarely cover. Additionally, university spin-outs historically faced heavy equity dilution, though recent data shows universities are taking smaller stakes to help founders raise money. The Demand Signal Industry leaders emphasize that the core issue is not a lack of engineering talent, but a shortage of local customers willing to install industrial equipment and buy production parts at scale. Without a robust domestic installed base, companies face higher training costs and often look to international markets, particularly the US, for growth. Experts suggest that clearer government procurement signals and stronger public-private co-investment could help bridge this gap.

item.title: US companies race to upgrade solar panel recycling and recover valuable silver
item.description: The looming waste wave According to the International Energy Agency, the annual volume of retired crystalline silicon solar modules in the US is projected to reach 87,000 metric tons by 2030 and skyrocket to 820,000 metric tons by 2050. Analysts at Rystad Energy estimate that the global value of recycled solar materials will hit $2.7 billion in 2030, surging to $80 billion by 2050. While glass and aluminum make up the vast majority of a panel's weight, silver used in the cells represents a major economic and strategic asset, having been added to the US Critical Minerals List in late 2025. Moving beyond shredding Traditional recycling systems rely on mechanical shredding, which often exports valuable metals trapped inside encapsulants and produces impure glass unsuitable for high-end manufacturing. To capture these values locally, several US companies are introducing new technologies. We Recycle Solar plans to open a critical materials recovery facility using regenerative solvents by 2027. Similarly, OnePlanet Solar is deploying its PRISM process to yield high-purity glass and silicon, while Comstock Metals is operating a facility in Nevada to decompose adhesives before extracting valuable metals without conventional smelting. Supply chains and regulation Success in this emerging sector relies heavily on partnerships with manufacturers and developers, such as agreements made by Solarcycle with major players like Qcells and Sunrun. Meanwhile, the regulatory landscape remains fragmented. Only four states currently ban solar panels from landfills, prompting companies to differentiate themselves through industry certifications such as the R2v3 standard and SEIA program participation to prove their traceability and environmental compliance.

item.title: OpenAI Expands Free ChatGPT Access Program for 200,000 Researchers
item.description: According to OpenAI News: Program Expansion OpenAI announced the expansion of its ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program, aiming to reach a total of 200,000 researchers globally. The next application round opens on November 23, offering 50,000 new grants on a first-come, first-served basis. Each grant covers the primary recipient and up to two collaborators with free access to ChatGPT Plus. Pilot Insights and Impact According to an OpenAI Economic Research report based on 1,800 participants from the summer pilot, surveyed researchers estimated that AI tools helped cut research time in half while maintaining quality. Early participants are utilizing the technology for various applications, such as identifying drug targets for tuberculosis and converting museum specimens into searchable 3D databases. Broader Access Initiatives In addition to individual researcher grants, OpenAI provides broader institutional access through ChatGPT Edu for universities and the GPT-Rosalind plan for biology labs. The company also contributed $5 million to a Simons Foundation initiative to support mathematical research using AI.

item.title: AI wipes out $206 billion in market value for 10 listed companies
item.description: The Scope of AI Disruption A new report by European Internet Ventures highlights that 10 listed companies operating in AI-exposed sectors saw their combined market capitalization plummet from $305 billion to $99 billion between December 2021 and November 2026. While nine of these businesses actually recorded revenue growth during parts of this period, investors are increasingly worried about long-term earnings as generative AI reshapes their foundational business models. Sector Breakdown The disruption hits hardest in industries built around information discovery and content creation. In travel, Tripadvisor's market value fell 77% and Trivago dropped 67% as AI assistants began comparing options directly, though Booking Holdings gained 20% due to its role in final payment processing. In creative and freelance sectors, companies like Shutterstock and Fiverr suffered steep valuation losses as users turned to AI for instant images and digital services. Meanwhile, education and developer platforms like Chegg and Stack Overflow faced massive declines as AI chatbots replaced subscription-based homework help and coding Q&A. Future Resilience The report suggests that platforms merely providing leads or information are vulnerable, while businesses that facilitate actual financial transactions and deliver end-to-end outcomes in fields like customer service and legal work may prove more resilient moving forward.

item.title: IBM Shows Progress in Bringing Quantum and HPC Together at SC26
item.description: According to IBM Quantum: Quantum-HPC Integration IBM, Cleveland Clinic, and RIKEN are finalists for the 2026 ACM Gordon Bell Prize after simulating protein-ligand complexes of up to 12,635 atoms using a combination of quantum processors and classical supercomputers. By breaking complex molecules into clusters, the team solved difficult parts using sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) alongside classical HPC methods. Platforms for Error Correction To tackle error correction, IBM partnered with ORNL and AMD to launch a co-design platform that places classical hardware directly next to physical qubits in Poughkeepsie, New York. Additionally, IBM and AMD released Pelagos, an open-source framework written in Triton that accelerates quantum error correction decoder tests on GPUs up to 97 times faster than standard CPU execution. Workflow Management Supercomputing centers rely on schedulers like Slurm to manage tasks. IBM and NVIDIA are integrating the open-source Quantum Resource Management Interface (QRMI) with Slurm's features, allowing researchers to request quantum processing units in job scripts just like they would request traditional GPUs or CPUs.

item.title: Riton releases M-100P micro metal 3D printer with 10-micron laser spot
item.description: According to Nanjixiong, Riton 3D released the M-100P micro metal 3D printer on November 17, 2026, pushing selective laser melting into a micrometer-scale territory. Core Technology Equipped with a self-developed ultra-fine laser and optical system, the M-100P achieves a 10-micron laser spot, a 15-micron melt track width, and a +/- 2-micron repetition accuracy. Its build volume is 100 mm in diameter by 80 mm in height. By combining closed-loop slicing algorithms with high-speed galvanometer scanning, the company reports that the printing speed is twice as fast as comparable systems, while yield strength and tensile strength increase by 15% to 25% due to finer grain structures. Applications and Impact The equipment supports stainless steel, titanium, and cobalt-chromium alloys, targeting high-value applications such as structural heart stents, medical puncture needles, and micro-electronic components. By reducing surface roughness and minimizing spatter, it bypasses heavy post-processing, offering an efficient alternative to traditional high-cost micro-machining.

item.title: Stark Future and Farsoon Team Up to Build Metal 3D Printing Production Line
item.description:
According to Farsoon Technologies 华曙高科:
Stark Future and Farsoon Technologies have entered an agreement at Formnext 2026 to implement multiple Farsoon FS4X metal additive manufacturing systems, creating a dedicated high-volume series production line. The collaboration extends beyond equipment installation, involving joint development of an end-to-end workflow that covers material parameters, heat treatment, downstream finishing, and full part traceability to reduce scrap and downtime.
At the center of this initiative is the Farsoon FS4X, a metal laser powder bed fusion platform designed for industrial series production with multi-laser processing and stable build conditions. This new venture scales up a partnership that began in 2024 when Stark Future utilized Farsoon's large-format printing platform, following milestones such as the KLINGA project which validated titanium serial production across more than 1,000 parts. According to Stark Future CEO Anton Wass, metal 3D printing allows the company to reduce component weight by up to 50% while optimizing vehicle performance.

item.title: Cohere introduces Video Intelligence in Compass for enterprise video search
item.description: According to Cohere Blog: Background Enterprises store vast amounts of information in recorded meetings, training sessions, and media archives, but videos have traditionally been difficult for AI applications to search effectively compared to text documents. Details Cohere's new Video Intelligence feature in Compass analyzes both spoken words and on-screen visuals. Instead of matching keywords in transcripts alone, it determines exact start and end times to answer user queries with precise clips, transcripts, and visual descriptions. It integrates video into the same retrieval system as documents, featuring permission-aware access control. According to Cohere's evaluations across 11 datasets, Compass ranks first on average with an nDCG@10 score 4.4 points ahead of alternative models. Impact The tool aims to unlock video data for enterprise retrieval-augmented generation and agentic workflows, with applications spanning recorded meetings, education, sports archives, and compliance review.

item.title: Johnson & Johnson to buy Ollin Biosciences for $2.2 billion upfront and partners with Blackstone
item.description: Acquisition Details Johnson & Johnson is paying $2.2 billion upfront to acquire Ollin Biosciences, alongside up to $1.125 billion in potential milestone payments. This move comes as J&J aims to rebuild its ophthalmology pipeline following recent setbacks, including handing back rights to a failed gene therapy and axing an experimental geographic atrophy treatment. Clinical Asset The central asset in the buyout is Ollin’s OLN324, a next-generation bispecific antibody targeting retinal diseases like wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema. According to Ollin, mid-stage trial data showed that OLN324 demonstrated faster and greater improvements in retinal anatomy and vision gains compared to a major competing therapy. Blackstone Funding Partnership To support the late-stage development of OLN324, J&J has enlisted private equity firm Blackstone Life Sciences. Blackstone will pay J&J $750 million over several years to fully fund the upcoming Phase 3 trials, in exchange for regulatory and sales milestone payments plus single-digit royalties.

item.title: 60-Megawatt Cooling Design for AI Data Centers Uses Dry Coolers Instead of Cooling Towers
item.description: System Architecture and Load Distribution Daikin Applied introduced a reference architecture named D60-W, sized for a 60-megawatt IT load and built on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform with NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72. The total load is split across six deployable units, with 92% cooled by liquid and 8% cooled by air. The setup uses two temperature loops, where a high-temperature liquid loop feeds coolant distribution units and a separate low-temperature loop serves air-cooling rack containment units. Cooling Modes and Water Savings Outdoor weather conditions determine whether the system operates in full mechanical, hybrid, or dry cooling mode. During dry mode, chiller compressors remain off, and heat is expelled through dry coolers instead of evaporative cooling towers. Daikin states this approach eliminates the need for make-up water, helping maintain low water usage effectiveness. Timeline and Scalability Capacity can be increased incrementally as demand grows since the design scales one deployable unit at a time. However, some key components, including Daikin's own coolant distribution unit and data center dry cooler, are still in development and scheduled for release in the second half of 2027.

item.title: US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely
item.description: Background The U.S. Commerce Department is rolling out an interim rule designed to close loopholes in existing export restrictions. Previously, rules required licenses only for shipping chips directly to companies in embargoed countries like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. However, companies have increasingly turned to remote-access loopholes, using overseas data centers to train advanced models. Key Details The new rule applies to any data center or network exceeding a specific computing power metric of 12 million total processing performance, roughly equivalent to about 750 Nvidia H100 or H200 chips. Operators must obtain licenses within 90 days if they serve customers from restricted countries. Additionally, the rule introduces new licensing requirements for semiconductor transfers to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil due to a higher risk of diversion, though chips destined for U.S.-based companies in these nations are exempt. The framework also rescinds the previous administration's AI Diffusion Rule. Industry Impact This regulatory shift forces global cloud and data center operators to strictly monitor customer ownership structures and network access. It comes in the wake of heightened scrutiny over Chinese firms scrambling for overseas compute capacity and aims to block actors from leveraging U.S. advanced semiconductors for intelligence-related or military activities.

item.title: Sakana AI Releases JFinBench: A Japanese Financial Benchmark Based on Latest Certification Exams
item.description: According to Sakana AI: Background and Motivation As large language models take on more specialized roles, specialized benchmarks are becoming crucial for reflecting real-world capabilities. While fields like software coding have seen open-weight models nearly match proprietary ones, domains requiring localized, frequently changing knowledge—such as Japanese finance and tax systems—lack robust evaluation standards. Existing benchmarks often rely on US systems or outdated exams. Benchmark Construction JFinBench comprises 321 questions sourced from six top-tier Japanese financial certification exams held in 2026, including certified public accountants and tax accountants. To tackle the challenge of converting complex PDFs into structured data, Sakana AI introduced a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline. Coding agents handled the heavy lifting of parsing layouts and formatting, while human experts verified all questions in about 12 hours total. Evaluation Insights Testing 12 prominent models showed that proprietary models like Claude Fable 5 and GPT-6 Astra dominated the top tiers. The best open-weight model, Kimi K3.1 Pro, scored significantly lower, highlighting a gap not visible in general coding benchmarks. The primary reason for failure was insufficient regulatory knowledge rather than arithmetic mistakes. Equipping models with external web tools helped bridge the gap, yet a performance deficit between open and proprietary models remained.

item.title: Biogen inks $411M neurodegeneration pact with protein degrader biotech TrimTech
item.description: Collaboration Details Biogen has entered into a biobucks agreement with U.K.-based TrimTech worth up to $411 million, which includes $32 million in upfront and research milestone payments. Under the pact, Biogen secures an exclusive global license to small molecule protein degraders developed through TrimTech's proprietary platform. Technology and Targets TrimTech focuses on using the E3-ligase TRIM21 to clear disease-causing protein aggregates. Its approach features bispecific chimeric molecules called TRIMTAC and mutual binding facilitator TRIMGLUE, offering an alternative to standard PROTACs. The company targets neurodegenerative conditions such as Huntington’s, Alzheimer’s, and Parkinson’s. Industry Context Founded in 2023, TrimTech previously raised a $47 million seed round involving major players like Johnson & Johnson, Eli Lilly, and Pfizer. This new agreement reinforces the growing interest from major drugmakers in targeted protein degradation for challenging diseases.

item.title: AI model detects small fires and smoke in PV plants
item.description: Background While deep learning has been widely applied in photovoltaic (PV) inspections for crack detection and hot-spot localization, dedicated fire detection in PV environments has rarely been explored. Details and Performance Developed by China Huaneng Group, the system integrates a custom annotated corpus named PV-Fire, which contains 5,824 images gathered from operating utility-scale plants and controlled outdoor burns. Based on the YOLOv12 model, the framework incorporates a patch-aware attention block, a multi-level gather-and-distribute mechanism, and an adaptive fusion head to spot weak flames and tiny smoke plumes. In benchmarks, PVFire-YOLO reached an mAP@50 of 87.4% on its native dataset, lowered the reflection-related false-positive rate down to 3.1%, and ran at 79 frames per second on a desktop GPU. Outlook The researchers state that future work will expand the image corpus to cover diverse climates, introduce temporal filtering to minimize isolated false positives, and combine visible light detection with infrared thermal imaging.

item.title: Novo’s CagriSema drives more than 20% weight loss at lower doses
item.description: Clinical Trial Results Novo Nordisk reported data from the Phase 3 REDEFINE 9 trial at the ObesityWeek 2026 conference. Patients receiving weekly doses of 1 mg and 1.7 mg of CagriSema lost 21% and 20.7% of their body weight, respectively, at week 68. These findings demonstrate that meaningful efficacy can be achieved below the previously studied highest dose. Background and Market Context CagriSema combines the amylin analog cagrilintide and the GLP-1 receptor agonist semaglutide. Earlier data from the REDEFINE 1 trial showed 22.7% weight loss at higher doses, which initially disappointed investors who had expected even higher figures. Despite previous setbacks, including failing to beat Eli Lilly’s Zepbound in a head-to-head test, Novo Nordisk continues to position the drug as a major next-generation therapy. Regulatory Outlook and Tolerability The latest findings form part of a broader data presentation as the drug awaits a U.S. FDA decision expected by the end of 2026. Analysts noted that tolerability remained consistent with previous studies, showing common side effects such as nausea and vomiting, while the company prepares to leverage its extensive clinical data to enter the market.

item.title: University spin-out turns internal lab tool into JetForge 3D printer
item.description: Background and Origins Founded by Richard Hague, Chris Tuck, and Ricky Wildman, Added started as a contract research business to handle industrial projects that did not fit a traditional academic schedule. Over time, the team focused on material jetting and binder jetting, building custom equipment when commercial prototyping machines proved too restrictive for testing new inks. The JetForge Platform Commercial 3D printers often lock users into a single manufacturer's materials, while typical development systems can be difficult to operate and maintain. JetForge solves this by packing the driver board, recirculation pump, and printhead into a removable module called a Blade. Users can swap these modules or run different heads simultaneously, configuring the machine for specific experimental needs such as multi-material printing or droplet inspection. Applications and Outlook The founders see immediate opportunities in electronics, such as printing conductive circuits directly through the body of polymer components or onto wearables. Added also collaborates with industrial partners on projects like desalination filter spacers and pharmaceutical oral dosage forms, aiming to help researchers quickly test and customize new materials.

item.title: Flatiron Energy starts construction on a massive 1.2GWh battery storage project in Massachusetts
item.description: Project Overview US energy storage developer Flatiron Energy has officially broken ground on the Energizar Energy Storage Project in Chelsea, Massachusetts. Flatiron states that the facility will feature a capacity of 250MW/1,200MWh, making it the largest battery energy storage system in the Northeast and one of the largest urban BESS facilities globally. Financing and Construction In October, Flatiron secured approximately US$850 million in financing for the project, covering construction loans, term loans, equity commitments, and tax credit transfers. Consigli Construction Co. is leading the construction work, with commercial operations scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027. Local Impact and Grid Role The facility aims to support the Greater Boston region by storing electricity during low-demand periods and releasing it during peak hours to improve grid reliability. Additionally, Flatiron is investing in local green economy programs, workforce development, and providing emergency response training for the local fire department.

item.title: Eli Lilly secures 1.5 billion dollar deal for Calytrix Bio to expand blood cancer pipeline
item.description: Eli Lilly is further expanding its footprint in the treatment of rare blood cancers by striking a deal worth up to $1.5 billion for Calytrix Bio, a biotech founded by J.P. Morgan's life sciences venture capital arm. The acquisition centers on a preclinical biparatopic antibody designed to target mutant calreticulin, which drives conditions like essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis. Unlike current therapies that primarily manage symptoms, this approach aims to provide disease-modifying activity. Citi analysts noted that the asset strategically complements Lilly's existing pipeline assets, though they cautioned that the program is still in the preclinical stage and faces a high safety bar. This transaction caps off a busy year of multibillion-dollar acquisitions and licensing agreements for Lilly, fueled largely by the strong sales of its GLP-1 drugs.

item.title: Canada pitches its biotech sector to Europe as U.S. political uncertainty grows
item.description:
U.S. political instability and uncertainty surrounding institutions like the FDA and NIH have prompted Canadian biotechs and contract research organizations to look beyond the United States. According to industry representatives at the BIO-Europe conference in Cologne, Germany, Canadian firms are actively promoting their strengths to European partners, aiming to secure licensing deals, co-development partners, and clinical collaborations.
On the opening day of the conference, three Canadian and Belgian health organizations—BioQuébec, Bioscience Association Manitoba (BAM), and BioWin—signed a trilateral Memorandum of Understanding to boost business development and knowledge exchange. Industry stakeholders note that Canada offers distinct advantages, including 30-day clinical trial application reviews by Health Canada, tax incentives, and a strong presence in emerging fields like AI-driven drug discovery and cell therapies.

item.title: Altera, OQC and NVIDIA Link Quantum Processor to GPU Computing
item.description: Background As quantum computers grow in scale, the number of qubits is increasing much faster than the physical space available for the traditional control equipment around them. This creates a bottleneck where control hardware needs to become significantly denser. Details According to Altera, the new end-to-end reference design is built on an Agilex 9 Direct RF FPGA. The FPGA handles real-time system control, qubit initialization, and resonator readout, communicating directly with an OQC quantum processing unit through specialized RF electronics. Meanwhile, NVIDIA NVQLink connects the FPGA to NVIDIA GPUs, which take over heavy computational tasks such as system calibration and machine learning-based readout classification using CUDA. Impact This collaboration provides developers with a validated software stack and a built-in emulation path to test algorithms before physical hardware is ready. The system is scheduled for a live demonstration at Supercomputing 2026 in Chicago, with the commercial release expected in January 2027.

item.title: Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?
item.description:
Remedy Robotics was founded by clinician David Bell and engineer Jake Sganga to tackle a stark medical reality: only about 1 in 10 eligible patients receive mechanical thrombectomies for acute ischemic strokes, largely because life-saving procedures are concentrated in major urban centers. Traditional stroke surgery requires physicians to manually thread a wire and catheter through narrow blood vessels while relying solely on a flat, two-dimensional X-ray, making it a blind and physically demanding task.
To bridge this gap, Remedy developed the N1 System, which features a steerable catheter driven by a robotic arm and guided by computer-vision software. The system translates basic directional commands from a controller into precise movements while overlaying 3D CT scans onto X-ray feeds. After successful preliminary tests on silicone models and a small nonemergency human trial in Toronto, the company recently secured $62 million in funding to advance upcoming clinical trials within the University of California system.
Despite the technological progress, widespread adoption of telesurgery faces steep hurdles. Experts point out that successful remote operations depend heavily on reliable network infrastructure, as rural areas often suffer from high latency that can disrupt surgical timing. Additionally, smaller hospitals frequently lack the necessary on-site medical staff, specialized intensive care units, and supporting equipment needed to handle complex stroke emergencies safely.

item.title: Google Maps updates Ask Maps with travel planning and local appointment booking
item.description:
According to Google AI:
According to Google Maps Product Director Maz Khorasani, the latest update introduces several conversational capabilities designed for holiday travel and preparation. Itinerary Building and Route Tips Users can now build step-by-step trip itineraries by prompting Ask Maps, which generates day-by-day schedules with numbered map pins. These plans can be shared or exported to Google Docs. When heading out, users can view live traffic, business hours, and weather conditions, and dynamically add stops such as scenic viewpoints along the route. Additionally, new route tips provide information on parking, EV charging, tolls, and delays. Appointment Booking and List Search Leveraging new agentic capabilities, Ask Maps can search online and call local businesses to find available appointments for services like pet care, beauty, and auto repair. Furthermore, users can query their saved lists with specific constraints, such as finding a saved restaurant that can seat five people within the next 30 minutes. Availability and Regional Rollout These updates began rolling out on Android and iOS on November 16, 2026. Ask Maps is also expanding to 30 European countries, including Spain, Germany, and the U.K., bringing availability to over 200 countries and territories. While travel itineraries and list search are available globally, the 'know before you go' route tips and appointment-finding features are launching first in the U.S.

item.title: Helus' Psychedelic Depression Drug Succeeds in Phase 3 Trial But Faces Safety Scrutiny
item.description:
Helus Pharma announced that its psychedelic drug candidate, HLP003, showed positive results in a Phase 3 clinical trial for major depression. In the study, participants received one dose on the first day and a second dose three weeks later alongside standard antidepressants. At six weeks, the treatment group achieved a 19.5-point reduction on the MADRS depression rating scale, compared to an 11.9-point reduction in the placebo group. At 12 weeks, the effect was largely sustained, with a 16.9-point reduction for the treatment group versus 9.9 points for the placebo group, with all differences being statistically significant.
Despite the promising efficacy data, the trial recorded a number of serious adverse events. These safety concerns have raised questions regarding the risk-benefit profile of utilizing psychedelics for psychiatric conditions, a therapeutic avenue currently being explored by multiple companies in the biotechnology sector.
